feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Iteration 5 (wheel_track 0.10, controller kp 5.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.8, outer weights ±1.5, inner ±0.75, sensor_size 0.012, row at y=0.08 with ±0.06 spread) scored 386.35, the best so far. The oval finished 20 of 20 runs, the s-bend progress rose from 0.17 to 0.42, and the slalom still lost the line once per run at progress 0.10. Iteration 4 showed that raising ki to 0.3 did not reduce the s-bend drift (still 0.0609) and cut the oval finish rate to 0.85, so the s-bend limit is turn rate, not a steady bias. For this race I keep the controller at iteration 5's values, so your sensor_size change is the only variable. Decision rules for the next race: if the slalom still loses the line about once per run with the outer sensors reading near zero, keep sensor_size 0.016 and try a wider row of x=±0.07 at y=0.08 with the same weights. If the s-bend still leaves the track at max_error about 0.062 with line losses near zero, narrow wheel_track to 0.09 m. If steering_oscillation rises on the oval above about 0.3 while max_error stays low, return sensor_size to 0.012 and change sensor spacing instead.
requested_changes: If the slalom still loses the line about once per run with the outer sensors reading near zero after sensor_size 0.016, widen the row to x=±0.07 at y=0.08, keeping the weights at ±1.5 and ±0.75. Iterations 3 and 5 both show the slalom losing the line once per run at the ±0.06 spread, so the outer sensors need more reach.

If the s-bend still leaves the track at max_error about 0.061 to 0.062 m with line_loss_events near 0, change wheel_track from 0.10 to 0.09 m. Iteration 5 moved s-bend progress from 0.17 to 0.42 when wheel_track went from 0.12 to 0.10 m, and the oval stayed at 20 of 20 finishes, so a further step is likely to help.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3 on the oval after sensor_size 0.016, return sensor_size to 0.012 and keep the ±0.06 row, rather than widening further. Iteration 4 showed that extra authority lowers the oval finish rate, so the larger footprint should not add jitter if the sensing change is working as intended.
